{{Current events|year=2019|month=09|day=30|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War]]
**Islamist militants launch two attacks against foreign forces in [[Somalia]]. A [[U.S. military]] base in [[Baledogle Airfield|Baledogle]], [[Lower Shabelle]], is stormed by attackers using two [[car bomb]]s and guns, and an [[Italy|Italian]] peacekeeping convoy is targeted by additional bombs in [[Mogadishu]]. United States and Italian authorities both state no injuries occurred, although the [[suicide bombing]] against the Italian convoy destroyed a military vehicle and heavily damaged nearby buildings. [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility for both attacks. [https://www.newsweek.com/jihadists-storm-us-air-base-bomb-military-convoy-1462056 (Newsweek)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)|Yemeni Civil War]], [[Yemeni peace process]]
**The [[International Committee of the Red Cross]] says that the [[Houthi movement|Houthi]]s have unilaterally released 290 prisoners. The move is part of a peace agreement brokered in [[Stockholm]] by the [[United Nations]] in December. The Houthis call on their opponents to take a comparable step. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-49880517 (BBC)]
*The [[Swedish Navy]] formally relocates its headquarters back to the underground [[Muskö naval base]] on the island of [[Muskö]] after a 25-year absence. The move from [[Karlskrona naval base]] to Muskö is based on the calculation that only Muskö could withstand a [[Russia]]n attack, according to the [[Swedish Defence Research Agency]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/sep/30/swedish-navy-returns-to-vast-underground-hq-amid-russia-fears (''The Guardian'')]

;Business and economy
*The American clothing retailer [[Forever 21]] files for [[Chapter 11, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] and announces it will close up to 178 stores. [https://www.npr.org/2019/09/30/765699885/nothing-lasts-forever-21-discovers-another-clothing-chain-files-for-bankruptcy (NPR)]
*[[economy of France|French]] airline [[XL Airways France|XL Airways]] grounds all flights amid financial difficulties ahead of a bankruptcy hearing scheduled for Wednesday. [https://www.thelocal.fr/20190930/second-french-airline-faces-collapse-as-all-flights-grounded (The Local)]
*[[Slovenia]]n airline [[Adria Airways]] cancels all flights and files for bankruptcy. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-slovenia-adria/slovenias-adria-airways-files-for-bankruptcy-idUKKBN1WF1OL (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of Vanuatu]], [[2019 Papua protests]]
**At the [[United Nations]], the [[Prime Minister of Vanuatu]], [[Charlot Salwai]], calls for "action on [[West Papua (province)|West Papua]]". He was rebuffed by Indonesian diplomats. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/399952/vanuatu-pm-calls-for-un-action-on-west-papua (RNZ)]
*[[Iraq–Syria relations]]
**The main [[Iraq–Syria border|border crossing]] between [[Al-Qa'im (town)|Al-Qa'im]], [[Iraq]], and [[Abu Kamal|Albukamal]], [[Syria]], reopens. [https://www.dailystar.com.lb/News/Middle-East/2019/Sep-30/492562-iraq-syria-reopen-major-border-crossing-retaken-from-daesh.ashx (AFP via ''The Daily Star'')]

;Law and crime
*Eight alleged members of a [[far-right politics in Germany|far right]] [[terrorism in Germany|terror cell]] go on trial in [[Germany]]. The defendents, from [[Chemnitz]], are accused of plotting attacks against [[immigration to Germany|immigrants]] and "the economic establishment". The city saw [[2018 Chemnitz protests|far-right protests last year]] following the stabbing homicide of a [[Germans|German man]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-49877578 (BBC)]
*[[Morocco|Moroccan]] journalist Hajar Raissouni and her husband Rifaat al-Amin are each jailed for a year by a [[Rabat]] court for [[premarital sex]] and unlawful [[abortion]], with doctor Mohammed Jamal Belkeziz receiving two years for carrying an abortion out. Her lawyer claims the evidence was fabricated to dissuade Raissouni and others from criticising the [[Government of Morocco|government]]. Observers including [[Amnesty International]] criticise the verdicts. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/sep/30/moroccan-journalist-hajar-raissouni-jailed-abortion (''The Guardian'')]
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**[[Riot]]s erupt following a fire yesterday which killed an [[Afghan people|Afghan woman]] at [[Kara Tepe Refugee Camp|an overcrowded refugee camp]] on the [[Greece|Greek]] island of [[Lesbos]]. The camp in Moria houses 13,000 in tents and [[shipping container]]s but has facilities for only 3,000 residents. The [[Greek government]] declares it will step up transfers to the [[mainland Greece|mainland]] in response. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/sep/30/riots-at-greek-refugee-camp-on-lesbos-after-fatal-fire (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Peruvian constitutional crisis]]
**[[President of Peru]] [[Martín Vizcarra]] dissolves the [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|Congress]] and calls for snap elections. Lawmakers reject the proposal, suspend him from office and name [[Vice President of Peru|Vice President]] [[Mercedes Aráoz]] as acting president. The [[Peruvian Armed Forces]] continued to recognize Vizcarra as President of Peru and head of the armed forces. Popular protests backing the President takes place in the streets of [[Lima]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-49888117 (BBC)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/01/perus-president-dissolves-congress-to-push-through-anti-corruption-reforms (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/30/world/americas/peru-vizcarra-congress.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Science and technology
*Scientists say the largest [[iceberg]] in 50 years has broken away from [[Antarctica]]'s [[Amery Ice Shelf]]. The 1,636 sq km iceberg, known as D28, will continue to be monitored as it could pose a risk to shipping. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-49885450 (BBC)]
*A near-record snowstorm drops large amounts of snow in some parts of [[Alberta]], from September 27-30. 95 cm fell in [[Waterton Park|Waterton]], 50-60 cm fell in [[Lethbridge]], and over 27-32 cm fell in [[Calgary]]. Impacts were relatively mild, with power outages, and businesses closing. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/alberta/article-southern-alberta-blanketed-with-snow-after-three-day-storm-shuts-down/ (The Globe and Mail)]
